items.title: Inside the punishing conditions Carnival crew face on cruise ships
items.description: Passengers boarding a Carnival cruise ship are promised a world of endless food, relaxation and oceanic luxury. But for the crew who make these escapes possible, life is vastly different.

items.title: Gambling ad reforms at risk as Labor draws line on major changes
items.description: Labor is unlikely to entertain major changes to its gambling ad crackdown despite the bill being 'friendless' in parliament.

items.title: AI model used fake identities to deceive humans in a safety test 'unprompted'
items.description: The British government's AI Security Institute has released a report showing AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic had, in test conditions, engaged in "harmful activity directed at real people and organisations".

items.title: Labor's migration test looks different to Howard's
items.description: If stopping asylum seeker boats was the great immigration challenge in decades past, achieving a lower Net Overseas Migration (NOM) figure has become the new political test.

items.title: Is Jetstar's new bag policy really just following the rest of the world?
items.description: Jetstar says charging passengers to use overhead lockers brings it into line with many overseas low-cost airlines. But is "unbundling" fees and charges actually making it more expensive to fly budget?

items.title: Parents warned not to 'shy away' from NAPLAN results
items.description: Parents concerned about their children's latest NAPLAN results are being encouraged to foster a love of language at home.

items.title: Battery-powered households not signing up to 'virtual power plant' scheme
items.description: Thousands of households with batteries installed under the federal government's scheme are choosing not to sign up to be a so-called virtual power plant that sells stored energy back to the grid.

items.title: MPs to assess if Australia prepared for war as concerns over conflict grow
items.description: It is the first time since World War II that a formal plan will be proposed, reflecting increasing concerns of conflict breaking out in this region.

items.title: Wall Street debt binge could end in tears — and lost billions
items.description: Credit default swaps for US big tech companies are soaring to record highs. It means investors are fearful of a major Wall Street company collapse.

items.title: What the success of 'Michigan Mamdani' says about the future of the Democrats
items.description: Abdul El-Sayed's victory over Haley Stevens in the Democrats' Michigan primary race could shape the party's messaging to voters and how it responds to Donald Trump ahead of November's crucial midterms.

items.title: Woman arrested after four men stabbed in central London
items.description: A woman has been arrested after four people were stabbed in one of central London's busiest tourist hotspots on Wednesday.

items.title: We've never seen the Sun in this much detail before
items.description: The highest-resolution imagery of the Sun's surface ever taken reveals dizzying currents, and clues about our star's magnetic fields.

items.title: A year on, still no answers in missing couple plane mystery
items.description: One year after a couple left in a brightly coloured plane from a small Tasmanian airport, friends are still hoping for answers about their disappearance.

items.title: 'Marked increase' in peptide users utilising needle exchange facilities
items.description: Experts and advocates fear at-risk drug users could be left without safe injecting equipment and resort to syringe-sharing.

items.title: Gillian Anderson on how Nicole Kidman led her to take more risks
items.description: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma sees the X-Files star take on a beguiling role as a reclusive former final girl.

items.title: Can you tell which movies were filmed in Australia?
items.description: The Australian film industry has a long and rich history of pretending local sets are exotic places. Put your film knowledge to the test with our quiz.

items.title: Artists from remote Australia among winners at prestigious fashion awards
items.description: A unique partnership between a remote Northern Territory women's centre and an art studio in India has been recognised at in this year's prestigious National Indigenous Fashion Awards.

items.title: 'Christmas card scene': Snowy winters in regional NSW melting into history
items.description: New South Wales is in the middle of its 30th consecutive warmer than average winter — and a past staple of the season is rapidly vanishing.

items.title: Frustrated commuters endure three months of disrupted rail services
items.description: Queensland Rail says one third of trains are now off the tracks due to a growing maintenance backlog as commuters stare down the barrel of more long months of reduced services.

items.title: Court orders removal of pensioner's 'therapy' roosters over noise complaints
items.description: A disability pensioner has been ordered to remove his three consistently crowing pet roosters — which he considers to be "therapeutic animals" — from his property in regional South Australia.

items.title: Second Melbourne gym in two days targeted by arsonists
items.description: A building in Melbourne's inner west that houses a gym and martial arts facility has been significantly damaged by a fire police are treating as a targeted attack.

items.title: How a bitter firefighters' pay dispute turned toxic in Victoria
items.description: IBAC's Operation Richmond found former premier Daniel Andrews, his senior ministers and public servants breached codes of conduct during protracted negotiations over a firefighters' wage deal in 2016.

items.title: Australians cut ties with servos as EV record sales continue
items.description: Over the past year, electric car sales have tripled, as anxiety about fuel shortages and rising petrol prices continues.

items.title: Taxi drivers working 12-hour days amid fuel price rise
items.description: A taxi driver says he is driving 12 hours a day and considering a second job to make ends meet amid rising fuel prices.

items.title: Exiled Bangladesh PM vows to return despite facing death sentence
items.description: The 78-year-old fled to India in August 2024 by helicopter at the height of the student-led uprising that toppled her government.
